title: discovery script scans .shatter/cache/ artifacts, inflating candidate count ~2x
description:
The discovery script scans the entire project root including `.shatter/cache/harness/rust/crate-bridge/*/crate-shadow/src/`. These directories contain Shatter's own generated shadow copies of the project's source files — byte-for-byte duplicates created during harness synthesis.

Observed in pickpackit:
- Real project source: ~2,900 candidate files
- `.shatter/cache/**` duplicates: ~2,900 additional candidates
- Total reported: 5,861 candidates (~2× inflation)

Concrete harms:
1. Cluster population is doubled, misrepresenting the true scope of coverage gaps.
2. Representative-example selection is polluted — cache copies have very long absolute paths and compete with real source files for the top-3 slots per cluster.
3. Every subsequent shatter-advise or shatter-gaps run on any project where Shatter has previously run suffers this inflation silently.

The project cannot prevent this: `.shatter/` is written by Shatter itself.

## Resolved codebase facts

Traversal mechanism (`catalog/skills/shatter-advise/scripts/discover_hotspots.py:102–109`):

```python
_SKIP_DIRS = {".git", "node_modules", "vendor", "target", "dist", "build", "__pycache__"}

def discover_candidates(root: Path, languages: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
    for path in root.rglob("*"):
        if any(part in _SKIP_DIRS for part in path.parts):
            continue
```

Fix: add `".shatter"` to `_SKIP_DIRS` (line 102). The existing `any(part in _SKIP_DIRS for part in path.parts)` check already handles all depths — no loop changes needed. This excludes `.shatter/cache/`, `.shatter/seeds/`, and all other Shatter-managed subdirectories. No project source lives under `.shatter/`.

After changing `discover_hotspots.py`, run `scripts/build-plugins` — the script is bundled into the plugin and CI runs `scripts/check-plugins-clean`.
acceptance_criteria:
- `".shatter"` is added to `_SKIP_DIRS` in `discover_hotspots.py`.
- No path containing `/.shatter/` appears in the candidates list after the fix.
- Candidate count on pickpackit drops from ~5,861 to ~2,900 (tolerance ±50).
- Legitimate source files outside `.shatter/` are still discovered.
- `scripts/build-plugins` exits 0.

title: shatter diff: first-class diff-scoped exploration command
description:
# shatter diff: first-class diff-scoped exploration command

## Summary

Add a `shatter diff [<base-ref>]` command that runs Shatter exploration only
against functions that changed between `<base-ref>` and the current working
tree. This makes pre-commit and PR-CI workflows fast and focused: instead of
re-exploring an entire project, Shatter reads the git diff, identifies which
functions were added or modified, and explores only those.

## Implementation Note

This is a feature request to the Shatter team. The implementing agent has
access to the Shatter source code. Two key constraints guide implementation:

1. **Reuse existing function-boundary detection.** Shatter already parses
   function boundaries in Go, TypeScript, and Rust (to perform exploration).
   `shatter diff` must use those same parsers to map changed hunk line ranges
   to function identifiers — not a separate diff-only parser. This keeps
   language support in sync as the engine evolves.

2. **Reuse existing function-level exploration.** Shatter already has an
   internal primitive that explores a single function (invoked when a project
   wrapper calls `shatter`). `shatter diff` passes the diff-derived list of
   `<file>:<function>` targets to that same primitive. The observable contract
   is defined below; the internal API form (CLI subcommand, library call,
   etc.) is at the implementor's discretion.

## Problem

Currently, exploring a project requires running the full project-scoped
wrapper (`npm run shatter`, `task shatter`, etc.), which re-explores every
registered function. For pre-commit gates and PR review workflows:

- A developer changes 2–4 functions; Shatter re-explores 80+.
- CI on a PR re-explores the entire codebase on every push.
- Skills that wrap Shatter for pre-commit use must implement git diff parsing
  and per-function invocation themselves — a fragile, language-specific layer
  that belongs in Shatter, not in each downstream skill.

## Proposed Command

```
shatter diff [<base-ref>] [--staged] [--include-tests]
             [--output-dir <path>] [--format json|text] [--jobs <N>]
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<base-ref>` | auto-detect (see below) | A single git ref. `shatter diff` diffs this ref against HEAD using three-dot merge-base semantics. Do NOT pass a range; `origin/main`, not `origin/main...HEAD`. |
| `--staged` | off | Diff staged index against HEAD (`git diff --cached`). Mutually exclusive with `<base-ref>`. |
| `--include-tests` | off | Include test functions (excluded by default per language rules below). |
| `--output-dir <path>` | `.shatter/diff-run/<timestamp>/` | Directory for spec JSONs and `summary.json`. |
| `--format json\|text` | `text` | Stdout format. `json`: stdout is the `summary.json` body (machine-readable). `text`: stdout is human-readable progress and result lines. `summary.json` is **always** written to `<output-dir>` regardless of format. |
| `--jobs <N>` | 1 | Concurrent exploration workers. Accepted in v1 CLI; sequential implementation is acceptable for v1. |

`<base-ref>` and `--staged` are mutually exclusive; passing both exits 3.

### Base-ref auto-detection (when `<base-ref>` is omitted and `--staged` is not set)

Resolve in this order; use the first that succeeds:

1. `git merge-base HEAD @{u}` — merge-base with the tracking remote branch.
2. `git merge-base HEAD main` — if `main` exists locally.
3. `git merge-base HEAD master` — if `master` exists locally.
4. `git rev-parse HEAD~1` — previous commit.
5. None resolve → emit error on stderr, exit 3.

Emit the resolved base-ref SHA as the first line of `text` output. In `json`
mode, it appears as the `"base_ref"` field in `summary.json` on stdout. In
`--staged` mode, `"base_ref"` is the SHA of HEAD (the staged diff compares
the index against HEAD); `text` output emits it as
`"base: <sha> (staged against index)"`.

### Project root detection

Walk up from the invocation directory until `.git/` is found. Supported-language
markers (`Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`, `package.json`) are discovered relative to
the git root, using the same rules as `run-shatter`. No project wrapper
(`scripts.shatter`, `task shatter`, etc.) is required.

If no git root is found, emit an error on stderr and exit 3.

## Outcome Enum

Every function-level exploration result carries one of these outcomes (same
values used in the existing `shatter_outcomes` map in `summary.json` from full
project runs, as read by `discover_hotspots.py`):

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `explored` | Shatter fully explored the function; at least one execution path found |
| `partial` | Shatter explored the function but did not reach all branches (budget exhausted or some paths blocked) |
| `unsupported` | Shatter could not construct inputs or execute the function (opaque resource, missing derive, etc.) |
| `error_only` | Shatter ran the function but every execution threw an error; no successful paths found |

## Per-function Spec JSON

Each attempted function produces a `<slug>.spec.json` in `<output-dir>`. The
schema matches Shatter's existing per-function spec format (consumed by
`interpret-shatter-spec` and `report-shatter-issues`):

```json
{
  "target": "<function-name>",
  "file": "<relative-file-path>",
  "outcome": "explored | partial | unsupported | error_only",
  "reason": "<populated when outcome is unsupported or error_only; else empty string>",
  "cases": [
    {
      "label": "<short label>",
      "inputs": { "<param>": "<value>" },
      "output": "<return value or thrown error>",
      "path_condition": "<constraint expression, if available>"
    }
  ]
}
```

`cases` is an empty array when `outcome` is `unsupported` or `error_only`.

## Function-to-Slug Mapping

Each function's spec file is named `<slug>.spec.json`. Slug derivation:

1. Replace `::` (Rust impl method separator) with `__`.
2. Replace `.` (TypeScript/Go method separator) with `__`.
3. Replace `/` and `\` with `_`.
4. Replace any character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` with `_`.
5. Collapse consecutive `_` runs to a single `_`.
6. Truncate to 200 characters.
7. If two functions in the same diff produce the same slug, append `_2`, `_3`,
   etc. in diff order.

Examples:
- Go `UpdateProject` → `UpdateProject`
- Rust `ProjectHandler::update` → `ProjectHandler__update`
- TypeScript class method `UserService.getById` → `UserService__getById`
- Rust free function literally named `Foo__bar` and Rust impl method `Foo::bar`
  both produce `Foo__bar`; the second gets `Foo__bar_2`.

## What Shatter Must Do

### 1. Obtain the diff

Non-staged: `git diff --unified=0 <resolved-base-sha>...HEAD`
Staged: `git diff --unified=0 --cached`

Always use three-dot form for the non-staged case. The CI integration example
also uses three-dot semantics (passed as `<base-ref>` = `origin/main`, which
Shatter expands to `origin/main...HEAD` internally).

### 2. Identify changed functions

Parse the unified diff. Skip binary file diffs
(`Binary files a/... and b/... differ`) and submodule diffs (lines starting
with `Subproject commit`) — add those to the `skipped` list with
`"reason": "binary_file"` or `"reason": "submodule"`.

For each `@@` hunk, map the hunk's new-file line range to the enclosing
function using Shatter's existing language parsers (same parsers used during
exploration). A function is "changed" if any `+` line falls within its body,
or if it was added in its entirety.

**Go (`*.go`):**
- Match `func <Name>`, `func (<Receiver>) <Name>`, `func (<Receiver> *<Type>) <Name>`.
- Exclude `*_test.go` unless `--include-tests`.

**TypeScript / JavaScript (`*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `*.js`, `*.jsx`):**
- Match: `function <name>`, `async function <name>`, `const <name> = (`,
  `const <name> = async (`, exported arrow functions, and method definitions
  inside `class` blocks (qualified as `<ClassName>.<methodName>`).
- `get`/`set` accessors: include as `<ClassName>.get_<property>` /
  `<ClassName>.set_<property>`.
- Anonymous default exports (`export default function() {}`): include as `default`.
- Computed property names and decorator-renamed functions: skip (cannot
  resolve to a stable static name).
- Exclude `*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`, `*.test.js`, `*.spec.js` unless
  `--include-tests`.

**Rust (`*.rs`):**
- Match `fn <name>`, `pub fn <name>`, `async fn <name>`, `pub async fn <name>`,
  and impl-block methods. For impl methods:
  - `impl Foo` → `Foo::<fn_name>`
  - `impl<T> Foo<T>` → `Foo::<fn_name>` (drop generics)
  - `impl Trait for Foo` → `Foo::<fn_name>` (use the concrete type, not the trait)
- Exclude `#[test]`-annotated functions and `#[cfg(test)]` modules unless
  `--include-tests`.

**Unsupported extensions:** add to `skipped` with `"reason": "language_unsupported"`.
Emit one line per skipped extension to stderr (`text` format); include in
`skipped` array (`json` format).

### 3. Dispatch exploration

For each identified `<file>:<function>` pair, invoke Shatter's existing
function-level exploration primitive. The observable contract: the
`<slug>.spec.json` output for each function must be semantically identical to
what a full project run would produce for that same function.

### 4. Emit output

**Output directory layout:**
```
.shatter/diff-run/<timestamp>/
├── summary.json
├── parseConfig.spec.json
├── UpdateProject.spec.json
└── ProjectHandler__update.spec.json
```

All spec JSON files sit directly in `<output-dir>` alongside `summary.json`.

**`summary.json`:**

```json
{
  "base_ref": "<resolved-sha>",
  "head_ref": "<sha-of-HEAD-at-run-time>",
  "staged": false,
  "files_skipped": 2,
  "functions_found": 7,
  "functions_attempted": 7,
  "outcomes": {
    "explored": 4,
    "partial": 1,
    "unsupported": 1,
    "error_only": 1
  },
  "targets": [
    {
      "file": "src/parser.ts",
      "function": "parseConfig",
      "outcome": "explored",
      "cases_found": 6,
      "spec_path": ".shatter/diff-run/20260624T121500/parseConfig.spec.json"
    },
    {
      "file": "src/handler.go",
      "function": "UpdateProject",
      "outcome": "unsupported",
      "reason": "parameter type *sql.DB is not constructible",
      "cases_found": 0,
      "spec_path": ".shatter/diff-run/20260624T121500/UpdateProject.spec.json"
    }
  ],
  "skipped": [
    {
      "file": "src/generated.proto",
      "reason": "language_unsupported"
    },
    {
      "file": "vendor/lib.rs",
      "reason": "binary_file"
    }
  ]
}
```

Field definitions:
- `spec_path`: relative to the git root (not the invocation directory), so paths are stable regardless of where `shatter diff` is invoked within the repo.
- `files_skipped`: count of entries in `skipped` (file-level, never explored). For a renamed-with-changes file, the old path contributes 1 to `files_skipped`; the new path's functions contribute to `functions_found`.
- `functions_found`: functions identified from the diff in non-skipped files.
- `functions_attempted`: count of entries in `targets` (= functions that
  exploration was dispatched for; equals `functions_found` unless a function
  was filtered post-identification for an internal reason).
- `outcomes`: per-outcome count of entries in `targets`.
- `head_ref`: SHA of HEAD at run time (`git rev-parse HEAD`).

**`skipped` entries are file-level skips** (unsupported extension, deleted,
renamed-no-changes, binary, submodule). **`targets` entries are function-level
attempts** — a function in `targets` with `outcome: unsupported` means Shatter
attempted but could not explore it, not that it was skipped.

**`--format json` stdout:** emits the same content as `summary.json` on stdout.
`summary.json` is written regardless of format.

**Large-diff warning:** if `functions_found > 200`, emit a warning to stderr
before beginning exploration. Exit code is unaffected.

### 5. Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | All `targets` have `outcome` `explored` or `partial` |
| 1 | At least one `target` has `outcome` `unsupported` or `error_only` |
| 2 | `targets` is empty (diff had no functions: empty diff, all-deleted, all-skipped files) |
| 3 | Configuration or environment error: bad flags, unresolvable base-ref, no git root, CRLF detected |

If `targets` is empty but `skipped` is non-empty (e.g., diff touched only
`.py` files), exit 2.

**Windows CRLF:** if diff output contains `\r\n`, emit error to stderr and
exit 3. Do not silently corrupt boundary detection.

## Edge Cases

| Situation | Behavior |
|---|---|
| New file (all `+`) | Explore all public/exported functions. Apply test exclusion. |
| Deleted file | Add to `skipped` with `"reason": "file_deleted"`. No targets. |
| Renamed, no content change | Add to `skipped` with `"reason": "renamed_no_changes"`. |
| Renamed, with content change | Old path → `skipped` `"file_deleted"`. New path explored. `"file"` in spec JSON = new path only. |
| Partially changed function | Include entire function. Granularity is function-level. |
| Binary file in diff | Add to `skipped` with `"reason": "binary_file"`. |
| Submodule diff | Add to `skipped` with `"reason": "submodule"`. |
| Functions whose callees changed but function itself did not | Out of scope for v1. |

## Integration

### Pre-commit hook

```sh
#!/bin/sh
shatter diff --staged --format json > .shatter/diff-run/last.json
exit $?
```

Exit code 1 means some functions are unsupported. Whether that blocks the
commit is the hook author's policy; Shatter provides the exit code.

### CI on pull requests

```yaml
- name: Run shatter diff
  run: shatter diff origin/main --format json --output-dir shatter-diff-output/
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: shatter-diff-report
    path: shatter-diff-output/
```

(`origin/main` is the single ref; Shatter expands it to `origin/main...HEAD`
internally using merge-base semantics.)

### Downstream skills

Detect support before calling:
```bash
shatter diff --help 2>&1 | grep -q '\-\-staged' && HAVE_DIFF=1 || HAVE_DIFF=0
```

Fall back to per-function invocation only if unavailable.

## Out of Scope (v1)

- Transitive impact analysis (callers of changed functions). Future: `--transitive`.
- Cross-file semantic diff (behavioral changes in unchanged callers).
- Seed generation from diff results.
- Non-git VCS.
- Windows CRLF support. Exit 3 with a clear error; address in v2.
- `--max-functions <N>` cap flag. Future addition.
- Concurrent dispatch (`--jobs N > 1` accepted; sequential is acceptable in v1).
- Python, Ruby, and other languages beyond Go, TypeScript, Rust.

## Acceptance Checks

1. **Function scoping:** fixture repo with 5 Go functions; modify 2. Run
   `shatter diff main`. Read `summary.json`; confirm
   `functions_found == 2` and `targets` lists exactly the 2 modified function
   names. (Do not rely on `git diff --name-only` which lists files, not
   functions.)

2. **Staged mode:** stage changes to 1 function; leave 2 others unstaged. Run
   `shatter diff --staged`. Confirm only the staged function appears in
   `targets`.

3. **JSON format — stdout and file match:** run
   `shatter diff main --format json --output-dir ./run`. Confirm:
   (a) `jq .functions_found ./run/summary.json` returns the correct integer,
   (b) stdout equals `./run/summary.json` byte-for-byte (or structurally
   equivalent JSON).

4. **Exit codes:**
   (a) all `explored` → exit 0;
   (b) one `unsupported` → exit 1;
   (c) diff touches only `.proto` files → exit 2 (all skipped, targets empty);
   (d) `shatter diff origin/main --staged` together → exit 3.

5. **No wrapper required:** remove `scripts.shatter` from `package.json`. Run
   `shatter diff main`. Confirm run proceeds without error.

6. **Deterministic output:** run `shatter diff main --output-dir ./run1`, then
   `shatter diff main --output-dir ./run2` with no intervening changes. Compare:
   `diff <(jq 'del(.targets[].spec_path)' ./run1/summary.json) \
         <(jq 'del(.targets[].spec_path)' ./run2/summary.json)`
   Confirm outputs are identical (empty diff).

7. **Test exclusion:** modify a `*_test.go` file. Run without `--include-tests`;
   confirm test functions absent from `targets`. Run with `--include-tests`;
   confirm they appear.

8. **Slug collision:** create a Rust file with (a) a free function named
   `Foo__bar` and (b) an impl method `impl Foo { fn bar() }`. Both produce
   slug `Foo__bar`. Run `shatter diff main`. Confirm spec files are
   `Foo__bar.spec.json` and `Foo__bar_2.spec.json` — no collision, no lost file.

9. **New file:** add a Go file with 3 exported functions. Run `shatter diff main`.
   Confirm all 3 appear in `targets`.

10. **Deleted file:** delete a Go file. Confirm the deleted file appears in
    `skipped` with `"reason": "file_deleted"` and no entries in `targets`.

11. **Base-ref auto-detection:**
    (a) branch with tracking remote: confirm `base_ref` matches
        `git merge-base HEAD @{u}`;
    (b) no tracking remote, `main` exists: confirm `base_ref` matches
        `git merge-base HEAD main`;
    (c) no tracking remote, no `main`, no `master` — set up with
        `git remote remove origin && git branch -D main master`:
        confirm `base_ref` matches `git rev-parse HEAD~1`.

12. **Large diff warning:** use a script to generate a Go file with 201 exported
    functions and commit it as a new file (all `+` lines). Run
    `shatter diff HEAD~1`. Confirm a warning appears on stderr and exit code is
    0 or 1 (not 2 or 3). (An all-deletion diff would produce no `targets` and
    exit 2; use an all-addition diff to ensure `targets` is populated.)

13. **Binary file in diff:** commit a binary file, then modify it. Run
    `shatter diff HEAD~1`. Confirm the binary file appears in `skipped` with
    `"reason": "binary_file"` and does not appear in `targets`.

title: auto-discover *_for_tests() factories and concrete trait implementors when generating state constructors
description:
When generating a state constructor (e.g. `AppState`), Shatter does not scan for test factory methods or concrete trait implementors already provided by the project. A human wrote the entire `api/.shatter/generators/pickpackit.rs` generator by hand, manually discovering:

- `AuthRuntime::dev_for_tests(secret: impl Into<String>)` — dev-mode runtime using HMAC; takes one argument
- `StorageClient::for_tests()` — zero-arg no-op stub client
- `DeterministicAssistant` — a concrete `impl AssistantProvider` in `api/src/assistant.rs:102`

The `Arc<dyn AssistantProvider>` field is the hardest case: Shatter cannot construct any trait object without knowing a concrete implementor.

## Resolved codebase facts

Factory methods confirmed in pickpackit:
- `AuthRuntime::dev_for_tests` — `api/src/auth/validator.rs:61`, signature: `pub fn dev_for_tests(secret: impl Into<String>) -> Self`
- `StorageClient::for_tests` — `api/src/storage/mod.rs:101`, signature: `pub fn for_tests() -> Self` (zero args)

Concrete trait implementors for `AssistantProvider` (`api/src/assistant.rs`):
- `DeterministicAssistant` (line 102) — no constructor args; correct auto-discovery choice
- `OllamaAssistant` (line 141) — requires external config; not suitable as auto-generated default
- `OpenAiAssistant` (line 210) — requires API key; not suitable as auto-generated default

`ShatterNoopAssistant` (hand-written in the generator itself) is a workaround for this gap. Once auto-discovery resolves `DeterministicAssistant`, it can be removed from the generator.
acceptance_criteria:
AC1 — Factory method scanning:
- Shatter scans for methods matching *_for_tests, *_for_testing, *::stub, *::mock, *::noop on state parameter types.
- Factory methods with arguments are included: the generated call uses a clearly marked placeholder, e.g. AuthRuntime::dev_for_tests("TODO: replace with test secret").
- When multiple factory methods match for the same type, zero-arg is preferred; fewest parameters wins among argument-bearing; ties broken alphabetically by method name.

AC2 — Concrete trait implementor scanning for Arc<dyn Trait>:
- Shatter finds all concrete impl Trait for T types in the project.
- Ranking: (1) structs with zero-arg ::new() or Default::default() and no external-resource fields, (2) structs with zero-arg ::new() and non-IO fields, (3) structs requiring arguments. Ties broken alphabetically by type name.
- DeterministicAssistant (rank 1) is selected for AssistantProvider; OllamaAssistant and OpenAiAssistant (rank 3) are not.

AC3 — Annotated TODOs for unresolvable fields:
- Fields with no resolvable factory or implementor emit: // TODO(shatter): resolve <TypeName> — no factory method or trait implementor found

AC4 — Regression:
- Existing hand-authored api/.shatter/generators/pickpackit.rs is not broken.

title: no managed Postgres injection for sqlx targets — generator falls back to hardcoded localhost:55432
description:
Shatter has no mechanism to provide a live PostgreSQL database to Rust targets that require one, forcing users to run an external DB before the harness can execute.

The canonical sqlx integration-test setup pattern appears identically across pickpackit's test files and in Shatter's own generated generator:

```rust
let url = std::env::var("DATABASE_URL").expect("...");
let pool = PgPoolOptions::new().max_connections(5).connect(&url).await.expect("connect");
MIGRATIONS.get_or_init(|| async { sqlx::migrate!("./migrations").run(&pool).await }).await;
```

The generator at `api/.shatter/generators/pickpackit.rs` falls back to:

```rust
const DEFAULT_DATABASE_URL: &str = "postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit";
```

and uses `connect_lazy_with`, which defers the failure into the first fuzz iteration. This shows the engine recognizes it needs a DB URL but punts on providing one. The project has done everything it can: `DATABASE_URL` injection point, `sqlx::migrate!()`, test-focused helpers. The DB must come from the engine side.

## Source artifact

`api/.shatter/generators/pickpackit.rs` — `database_url()` function, `shared_pool()` function using `connect_lazy_with`, and `DEFAULT_DATABASE_URL` constant.

Generator is produced by skill/runtime guidance in `catalog/skills/interpret-shatter-spec/`.
acceptance_criteria:
Either (a) or (b) satisfies this issue:

(a) Managed Postgres mode:
- Shatter detects the PgPoolOptions + connect(DATABASE_URL) + sqlx::migrate!() setup idiom in Rust generators.
- Shatter provides a mode (opt-in via CLI flag or config key, or auto-detected) to launch a temporary Postgres container before the harness run (Docker primary; Podman-compatible if feasible).
- DATABASE_URL is exported into the harness process environment; sqlx::migrate!() runs automatically before first iteration. Container tears down after run.

(b) Minimum — early-exit with clear error:
- When DATABASE_URL is absent and no DB responds at the fallback URL, an actionable error fires before the first fuzz iteration (not inside a fuzz loop).
- connect_lazy_with is replaced with eager connect or a pre-flight connectivity check.
- Error message names the problem, the fix (e.g. 'run `make api-test-integration`'), and the env var to set.

title: crate-bridge harness uses synthetic /test/{p0}/{p1} path instead of real axum route
description:
When Shatter generates a crate-bridge harness for an axum handler, it mounts the handler at a synthetic path (`/test/{p0}/{p1}`) rather than the handler's real application route.

Observed in pickpackit: the generated `main.rs` for `handlers::create_bundle_entry` contains:

```rust
let app = Router::new()
    .route("/test/{p0}/{p1}", routing::any(pickpackit_api::handlers::create_bundle_entry));
```

The real route (from `api/src/app.rs` `build_router()`) is:
`/workspaces/{workspace_id}/bundles/{bundle_id}/entries`

Three concrete consequences:

1. Per-route middleware is missing. The real app applies `DefaultBodyLimit::max` on specific upload routes; the synthetic router never applies these layers.
2. Auth middleware is bypassed. The real router wraps `/api` with `ensure_account_layer` and `auth_layer`. The harness injects `CurrentAccount` directly via `request.extensions_mut()`.
3. Path parameter names diverge. Axum extracts `p0`/`p1` instead of `workspace_id`/`bundle_id`.

## Resolved codebase facts

- Real router: `api/src/app.rs`, `build_router()` — handler `create_bundle_entry` wired at `/workspaces/{workspace_id}/bundles/{bundle_id}/entries` (POST).
- Generated harness: `api/.shatter/cache/harness/rust/crate-bridge/<hash>/src/main.rs` (hash is content-addressed; regenerated when handler or generator changes).
- The harness is generated by Shatter's harness-generation machinery guided by skills in `catalog/skills/`. The skill/runtime producing `main.rs` is the fix target.
- The router uses nested composition: `Router::new().nest("/api", api)`. The `api` sub-router is where all handler routes live, behind the auth middleware layers.
acceptance_criteria:
Minimum — comment + TODO annotation:
- Generated `main.rs` includes a comment immediately adjacent to the `.route()` call: `// Real route: /workspaces/{workspace_id}/bundles/{bundle_id}/entries`
- A `// TODO(shatter): replace synthetic path with real route above` annotation appears on or directly below the `.route("/test/...")` line.

Ideal — static extraction:
- Shatter analyzes `build_router()` and uses the real path pattern in the generated `.route()` call.
- Default seed URL contains real parameter names and values.

Regression: for a handler with no matching route found, harness still generates valid Rust with a TODO, does not crash.

title: Track bento improvement proposals surfaced by shatter-agents design
description:
## Background

The shatter-agents design spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-16-shatterproof-marketplace-design.md`, section 5) explicitly diagnoses four weaknesses in bento's marketplace builder and implements superior alternatives here. These improvements should be proposed upstream to bento.

## Improvements to Propose

1. **Consistency gate**: Bento has no CI check that diffs committed `plugins/` against a fresh build. Drift accumulates silently. A `check-plugins-clean`-style gate (run build to temp dir, diff against committed output, exit nonzero on difference) should be added to bento's CI.

2. **Wipe-and-regenerate build**: Bento's builder does in-place reconciliation, which allows stale files to accumulate when skills are removed or renamed. Wipe-and-regenerate (delete `plugins/<target>/` entirely, then recreate) is simpler and eliminates stale-file bugs.

3. **Model hints in `metadata.json`**: Bento puts `recommended_model: low|mid|high` in SKILL.md frontmatter. This is Claude-specific, not part of the documented SKILL.md contract, and ages poorly. Moving it to `metadata.json` (as shatter-agents does) is strictly better for portability.

4. **Content-hash auto-versioning**: Bento uses a manual `bump-plugin-versions` script. Content-hash-based auto-versioning (keyed on a SHA-256 hash of sorted file paths + content) eliminates the class of "forgot to bump" bugs.

## Acceptance Checks

This is a tracking/planning issue. Resolved when:
- Proposals have been communicated to bento maintainers, OR
- It has been determined that bento will not adopt these improvements and this issue is closed as deferred

No code changes in this repo are required.

## In Scope

- Documenting and communicating the four improvement proposals to bento

## Out of Scope

- Implementing any of these in this repo (already done)

title: Fix doc-code mismatch: versioning auto-bump never resumes after patch=0
description:
## Symptom

`docs/conventions/versioning.md` states that after a manual major/minor bump to a version with `patch = 0`, "subsequent content changes resume the auto-bump at 2.0.1, 2.0.2, and so on." The code never does this. Once a human sets `patch = 0`, auto-bump is permanently disabled for that plugin.

## Code Facts

- File: `scripts/build-plugins`, function `bump_version_if_changed` (lines 205-219):
  ```python
  if patch == 0:
      new_version = old_version   # stays 0 forever
  else:
      new_version = f"{major}.{minor}.{patch + 1}"
  ```
  Every call with `patch == 0` keeps the version unchanged. There is no mechanism to transition out automatically.

- File: `docs/conventions/versioning.md`, paragraph "Manual major or minor bumps":
  "The next build sees the patch=0 anchor and records the new hash without auto-bumping; **subsequent content changes resume the auto-bump at 2.0.1, 2.0.2, and so on.**" — this is incorrect.

- `test_bump_version_keeps_version_when_patch_is_zero` in `tests/test_build_plugins.py` only covers the first content-change case. No test covers a second content change after a patch=0 anchor.

## Recommended Fix (Option A — fix the docs)

The current code behavior is defensible: patch=0 is a permanent anchor, not a one-time skip. Update `docs/conventions/versioning.md` to accurately say: all subsequent content changes leave the version pinned at the manual value; increment the patch manually when ready to resume auto-bumping.

Add a test for "second content change after manual bump with patch=0 still does not auto-bump" to make the invariant explicit.

(Option B — fix the code to match the doc — is also acceptable but requires tracking state across builds and is significantly more complex.)

## Acceptance Checks

- `docs/conventions/versioning.md` accurately describes patch=0 behavior
- A new test verifies that calling `bump_version_if_changed` twice with patch=0 and differing hashes never auto-bumps the version
- All existing tests continue to pass

- Changes to `catalog/plugin-versions.json`

title: Fix tmpdir resource leak in install/codex-home.sh
description:
## Symptom

Every network install via `curl ... | bash` leaks a temp directory under `/tmp/`. The directory is never cleaned up after the installer exits.

## Root Cause

`download_source()` declares `tmpdir` as a `local` bash variable (`#!/usr/bin/env bash`) and registers `trap 'rm -rf "$tmpdir"' EXIT` at line 49. After the function returns, `$tmpdir` is out of scope in the main shell (evaluates to empty). When `exec` replaces the shell at line 67, bash fires the EXIT trap and runs `rm -rf ''` — a no-op. The downloaded archive directory is left on disk.

## Code Facts

- File: `install/codex-home.sh`, shebang `#!/usr/bin/env bash`
- `local tmpdir` at line 47; `trap 'rm -rf "$tmpdir"' EXIT` at line 49
- `SOURCE="$tmpdir"` (global assignment) at line 58
- `exec "$SOURCE/scripts/install-codex-plugins" ...` at line 67
- The `SHATTER_AGENTS_SOURCE` path bypasses `download_source()` entirely; unaffected.

## Proposed Fix

Move cleanup to the global shell scope using a non-local variable:

```bash
_DOWNLOAD_TMPDIR=""
_cleanup() { [ -n "$_DOWNLOAD_TMPDIR" ] && rm -rf "$_DOWNLOAD_TMPDIR"; }
trap _cleanup EXIT

download_source() {
  _DOWNLOAD_TMPDIR="$(mktemp -d)"
  # ... download to $_DOWNLOAD_TMPDIR ...
  SOURCE="$_DOWNLOAD_TMPDIR"
}
```

## Acceptance Checks

- Running `install/codex-home.sh` with `SHATTER_AGENTS_SOURCE` pointing to a prepared directory (bypassing network) leaves no leftover directory under `/tmp/`
- `--source` / `SHATTER_AGENTS_SOURCE` path continues to work unchanged
- `test_bootstrap_uses_existing_source_without_network` still passes

## In Scope

- Fix the temp dir leak in `install/codex-home.sh`

## Out of Scope

- Changes to `scripts/install-codex-plugins`
- Testing the live network download path in CI

description:
Title: Add bounded Shatter tractability taxonomy spec

Type: task
Priority: 2

## Purpose

Add one documentation-only research/spec file to `shatter-agents`:

`docs/specs/2026-06-16-shatter-tractability-taxonomy.md`

The spec should turn the existing tractability note and this session's planning into a bounded taxonomy of project-side refactorings that make target code more tractable to Shatter exploration. It should be usable later as the conceptual base for a `shatter-agents` skill or recommendations engine, but this issue does not build that skill or engine.

## Current Code Facts

- Target repository: `~/project/shatter-agents`.
- `shatter-agents` is the shatterproof marketplace for Shatter and Refute plugins.
- Repo instructions say generated output under `plugins/` must not be edited by hand.
- Project documentation guidance says not to create new `docs/superpowers/...` paths; new project docs should use direct paths such as `docs/specs/`.
- Existing `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-16-shatterproof-marketplace-design.md` is historical and should not be used as the destination pattern for new docs.
- Source note: `~/shatter-tractability-recommendations-engine.md`. Treat its four-gate taxonomy and disposition model as authoritative seed material, then broaden it with the examples and patterns below.
- Bernhardt reference: Gary Bernhardt, "Functional Core, Imperative Shell", https://www.destroyallsoftware.com/screencasts/catalog/functional-core-imperative-shell. Use it as the organizing design lens; do not rely on long quotes.

## Required Spec Shape

Keep the document bounded to roughly 3,000-5,000 words. Use this outline:

1. `# Shatter Tractability Taxonomy`
2. `## Executive Summary`
3. `## Core Principle: Functional Core, Imperative Shell`
4. `## Tractability Gates`
5. `## Recommendation Dispositions`
6. `## Pattern Catalog`
7. `## Example Mapping`
8. `## Future Recommendations Engine`
9. `## Non-Goals`

## Required Content

The spec must include:

- The four gates: constructibility, executability, coverage depth, and measurement.
- The four dispositions: `PROJECT-FIX`, `ENGINE-GAP`, `CONFIG-TUNE`, and `JUSTIFIED-SKIP`.
- A clear distinction between general software design/testability advice and Shatter-specific automation constraints.
- Pattern sketches, not automated recipes.
- First-class Go, TypeScript, and Rust coverage.
- A future report vocabulary with at least: `pattern_id`, `tractability_gate`, `disposition`, `confidence`, `evidence`, `suggested_refactor`, `expected_coverage_gain`, `leverage_score`, `effort_estimate`, `manual_review_notes`, and `engine_issue_ref`.

The pattern catalog must cover these bounded categories:

- Functional core / imperative shell.
- Small project-owned ports or interfaces around opaque resources.
- Handler sandwich split: parse/auth/validate/core/effect/render.
- Query/result separation.
- Scenario/state factories for IO that must remain.
- Fixture sets across external decoder or FFI boundaries.
- Time/random/env/global extraction.
- Browser/runtime global isolation.
- Factory and closure capture for stores/builders/registries.
- Callback and streaming inversion.
- Concurrency shell extraction.
- Generated/framework glue avoidance.
- Serialization and validated-input boundaries.

## Required Example Mapping

Use exactly these examples as evidence; do not expand into a full audit of each project:

- Go/resource boundary: `~/project/refute/internal/backend/lsp/priming.go`, `PrimeWorkspace`, where a concrete LSP client can be treated as a small `DidOpen`-style interface boundary.

title: implement: recipe schema and stub-registration for independent per-parameter resource stubbing
description:
Implement the recipe schema and stub-registration mechanism for independent per-parameter resource stubbing in multi-parameter functions. The design is resolved in `docs/specs/2026-06-24-recipe-schema-design.md` (sa-mty). The four design questions are answered there; this issue implements those decisions as code.

## Resolved design facts (from sa-mty)

These are decided. Do not re-open them; implement them.

1. **Recipe schema (v1).** A JSON document:
   - `schemaVersion: 1` (reject unknown major versions).
   - `target`: source-path-relative `::` function id, e.g. `api/src/sweeper.rs::run_once`.
   - `bindings`: map keyed by **parameter name** (not type, not position).
   - Binding values: `"live"` / `{ "live": "<scenario>" }` / `{ "stub": "<name>", "with": {…} }` (shorthand `"stub:<name>"`) / `"default"` / `{ "value": <literal> }`; absent ⇒ default synthesis.
   - Recipes live at `.shatter/recipes/<target-id>/<recipe-name>.json`; one target may have many named recipes. `run-shatter` discovery enumerates them per target.

2. **Stub authoring & registration.** Stubs are project-owned source under `shatter/stubs/<lang>/`, gated out of release builds (Rust cfg/feature, Go build tag, TS dev-only entry). A stub implements the **port trait the target parameter is typed as** (port seam is a project prerequisite, taxonomy PROJECT-FIX) and exposes a factory. Discovery is a **config-declared registry**: a `stubs:` section in `.shatter/config.yaml` mapping `name → {implements, lang, source, factory}`. Also a `scenarios:` section mapping live scenario factories `name → {parameter_type, lang, source, factory}`. Attribute-based auto-discovery (`#[shatter::stub]`) is explicitly a future enhancement, NOT in v1.

3. **Generator interface placement.** Introduce a **new generator shape — the composed recipe generator** — that replaces the monolithic `State()` call ONLY when a recipe is attached. `State()` is unchanged and remains the default with no recipe. The composed generator resolves each binding independently and assembles the argument tuple at the input-construction stage, after target discovery and after recipe validation, before execution. Parameters bound to `default` are still varied by the concolic solver; `live`/`stub` parameters are held fixed for the run.

4. **Fallback behavior.** **Fail fast before the run** with a precise validation error — never silently substitute a default for an explicitly named stub. Validation runs before any resource construction/execution and errors on: unknown parameter key; unregistered stub name; stub `implements` ≠ parameter port type; concrete-typed parameter with no port seam; missing live setup/named scenario; unsupported `schemaVersion`. Absent bindings (and explicit `"default"`) use default synthesis — the only default path.

## Scope of implementation

- Recipe document parser + `schemaVersion` gate.
- Recipe validator producing the precise errors enumerated above, runnable before execution.
- `.shatter/config.yaml` `stubs:` and `scenarios:` registry parsing.
- The composed recipe generator and its insertion at the input-construction stage (gated on recipe presence; `State()` path untouched otherwise).
- Recipe discovery in the `run-shatter` target surface (`.shatter/recipes/<target-id>/*.json`).
- A worked reference: the pickpackit sweeper `s3-delete-fails` recipe, the `storage_delete_errors` stub, and the `rows_pending_delete` scenario, matching the design doc's sample verbatim.

## Acceptance criteria

- A target with no recipe behaves exactly as before (backward compatible).
- The pickpackit sweeper `s3-delete-fails.json` recipe resolves to a real seeded `PgPool` + erroring `Storage` stub and reaches the "rows left for retry" branch.
- Every validation error case in design fact #4 is covered by a test and fails before any target executes.
- An unknown `schemaVersion` and an unregistered stub name both error, not warn.

Blocked on sa-mty (design spike). See `docs/specs/2026-06-24-recipe-schema-design.md`.

title: design: recipe schema and stub-registration for independent resource stubbing in multi-parameter async functions
description:
This is a design-first feature issue. Implementation cannot begin until the design questions below are resolved — this issue IS the design spike.

## Problem

Functions that take multiple external resource handles as independent parameters cannot have each resource stubbed independently. Shatter's generator model produces one bundled state object with no mechanism to combine a real instance of one resource with a stub of another.

Observed in pickpackit's sweeper: `sweeper::run_once(pool: &PgPool, config: &SweeperConfig, storage: &StorageClient)`. Reaching the 'S3 delete fails, rows left for retry' branch requires a real PgPool returning rows PLUS a stub StorageClient returning errors on `delete_object`. The current model cannot express this.

Source artifact: `api/src/sweeper.rs` — `run_once` function signature.

## Design questions to resolve in this spike

1. Recipe schema: What does multi-resource stubbing look like in a recipe? Sketch: `{ "pool": "live", "storage": "stub_error" }` — but key naming convention (parameter name? type name? alias?), value format, and schema version are all undefined.

2. Stub authoring and registration: How does a project author a stub for a specific type (e.g. a StorageClient that errors on delete_object)? Where do stub files live? What is the interface/trait a stub must implement? How does Shatter discover registered stubs by name?

3. Generator interface placement: Does multi-resource composition extend the existing State() generator contract, or introduce a new generator shape? Where does the composed recipe get applied in the pipeline?

4. Fallback behavior: When a recipe specifies a stub name but no registered stub exists for that type, what happens? Error before run, or substitution with a default?

## Acceptance criteria for this spike

- The four design questions above each have a documented answer (in a design note or DESIGN.md update).
- The recipe schema is concrete enough that a sample recipe for the pickpackit sweeper case can be written out in full.
- A stub authoring example (a stub StorageClient that errors on delete_object) is sketched in code or pseudocode.
- A follow-on implementation issue is created with the design decisions filled in as resolved codebase facts.
notes: Self-blocking design issue. Do not claim for implementation until all four design questions are answered. The follow-on implementation issue should be blocked on this one via a dep link.

title: Async shell sync core refactor guidance
description:
# Skill detects async shell / sync core refactors

## Problem

The Shatter-related tractability/refactoring skill being built in `shatter-agents`
should treat async orchestration as a first-class refactoring pattern. Async
handlers and workers often mix framework/runtime awaits, external calls,
timers, cancellation or streaming concerns, and deterministic business logic in
one function. Shatter may not be able to exercise the async runtime shape, but
it can often cover the deterministic middle if the project extracts a sync core.

## Desired Behavior

When the skill analyzes target project code, it should be able to recommend an
`ASYNC-SHELL-SYNC-CORE` pattern, or equivalent name:

- Keep async code at the boundary for parse/load/effect/render operations.
- Convert awaited inputs into plain project-owned data before the core call.
- Extract deterministic decision logic into a synchronous project-owned helper.
- Return a result, plan, or command object from the sync helper.
- Let the async shell perform the awaited effects after the core returns.

The recommendation should distinguish incidental async orchestration from
behavior whose essence is async: scheduling order, cancellation races,
backpressure, task interleavings, runtime-specific behavior, or streaming
protocol semantics.

## Current Code Facts

- Repo: `shatter-agents`.
- Existing tracker issue `agents-2b3` refers to a `shatter-tractability-improver`
  skill in design that will recommend or apply `PROJECT-FIX` refactorings.
- The landed taxonomy spec is
  `docs/specs/2026-06-16-shatter-tractability-taxonomy.md`.
- A bounded search of that spec found no explicit `ASYNC` pattern token, so
  this issue records the async-specific refinement rather than assuming it is
  already covered.
- Repo rules say canonical plugin/skill sources live under `catalog/`; generated
  `plugins/` output must not be edited by hand. If this work changes canonical
  skill text, run `scripts/build-plugins` and verify `scripts/check-plugins-clean`.

## Acceptance Checks

- The Shatter-related tractability/refactoring skill guidance includes an
  explicit async-shell/sync-core recommendation pattern.
- The pattern explains when the disposition is usually `PROJECT-FIX` versus
  `ENGINE-GAP`, `CONFIG-TUNE`, or `JUSTIFIED-SKIP`.
- The pattern calls out that a trivial async wrapper is useful only when the
  sync core takes ordinary data, avoids hidden IO/globals/runtime handles, and
  returns ordinary data, a plan, or commands.
- The guidance includes at least one compact sketch showing an async wrapper
  around a sync core.
- Generated plugin output, if any, is produced through `scripts/build-plugins`;
  `scripts/check-plugins-clean` passes after the change.

## In Scope

- Add guidance for recognizing and recommending async-shell/sync-core
  refactors in the currently-being-built Shatter tractability/refactoring skill.
- Optionally add or cross-reference the same named pattern in the taxonomy spec
  if that is the skill's source of truth.

## Out of Scope

- Implementing async runtime support in Shatter core.
- Promising automated refactoring for scheduler, cancellation, backpressure, or
  streaming behavior.
- Broad async audits of target projects.

title: refute: add extract-function and move-to-module operations
description:

The most common patterns require operations beyond rename: extracting a pure helper function from a mixed handler, moving a block of logic into its own module, and splitting a handler sandwich into boundary/core/effect layers.

Needed operations:
- extract-function: select a range of code, give it a name, replace with a call — driven via LSP code-action or direct text manipulation with symbol awareness
- move-to-file/module: move a named function/type to a new or existing file, updating all references
- inline-variable: collapse a single-use binding (useful cleanup after extract)

These mirror standard LSP code actions (Extract Function, Move to new file) supported by gopls, rust-analyzer, and typescript-language-server.

Until this lands, the tractability-improver skill will generate proposed code sketches and diffs for human/agent review rather than applying them automatically. This issue tracks the refute side of closing that gap.

title: Trim bd context injection: .beads/PRIME.md override + memories-only PreCompact + minimal setup block
description:
bd prime injects ~768 words (~1,220 tokens) of mostly static workflow boilerplate at every Claude Code SessionStart, and again at every PreCompact, in any repo with a beads workspace (the beads plugin auto-runs it; some repos also wire it explicitly in .claude/settings.json). bd ships the fix as a supported customization point (see `bd prime --help`): a `.beads/PRIME.md` file overrides the default output entirely; `bd prime --export` dumps the default for editing; `bd prime --memories-only` emits only persistent memories (~45 words).

Work:
1. `bd prime --export > .beads/PRIME.md`, then trim to ~150-200 words keeping only: the condensed session-close checklist (status/add/commit/push), the six core commands (ready, show, create, update --claim, close, dep add), the no-TodoWrite and `bd remember` rules, and a closing pointer ("run `bd prime --full` for the complete reference").
2. Check this repo's `.claude/settings.json` (and be aware of the user-global one) for explicit bd prime hook wiring; where a PreCompact hook runs `bd prime`, switch it to `bd prime --memories-only` — after compaction the summary carries workflow state, and memories are the only content genuinely at risk.
3. Verify before committing: does a PRIME.md override still append persistent memories to SessionStart output? (The help text says the override replaces output "entirely".) If memories are suppressed, either end PRIME.md with an instruction to run `bd memories`, or add `bd prime --memories-only` as a second SessionStart hook.
4. If this repo's AGENTS.md carries a `<!-- generated by bd setup codex -->` ... `<!-- END BEADS CODEX SETUP -->` block, shrink the content inside the markers to two lines: "This repo uses bd (Beads). Run `bd prime` before tracker work. This block is intentionally minimal — do not re-run `bd setup codex`." title: shatter-doctor skill
description:
Add a `shatter-doctor` skill to the shatter plugin in shatter-agents.

## Purpose

Agent-driven diagnostic of a project's Shatter setup. The skill performs the
diagnostic itself; it does NOT depend on a `shatter doctor` subcommand (no
such subcommand exists in Shatter).

## Audience

Downstream user. Run when Shatter is misbehaving in a project, when a user
is unsure whether the setup is correct, or before adopting Shatter in an
unfamiliar repo.

## Behavior

The skill should:

- Verify the `shatter` binary is installed and runnable. Report the version
  and (best-effort) compare against the published continuous-release
  manifest to flag stale installs.
- Check `.shatter/config.yaml` exists and parses; surface any schema
  errors observed during parsing.
- Run the same target-discovery helper that `run-shatter` uses
  (`scripts/run_targets.py --root <repo> --json`) and report, per
  detected target: whether it is integrated, the integration surface used
  (`package.json` script, Taskfile task, etc.), and the proximate reason for
  any `not integrated` verdict (no language manifest, missing wrapper,
  wrapper named something other than `shatter`).
- For non-integrated targets, point at the `add-shatter-target` skill (once
  that ships).
- For binary or install problems, point at the `install-shatter` skill.
- Stop short of running any actual Shatter exploration and stop short of
  modifying the project. Diagnosis only.

## Smallest concrete shape

User says "diagnose my Shatter setup". Skill prints:

- Binary: `shatter 0.x.y` (continuous-20260514-...; matches published manifest).
- Config: `.shatter/config.yaml` parsed OK / has errors at lines X.
- Targets: a small table — path, language, integrated/not, surface, reason.
- Recommended next steps as a short bullet list.

## Acceptance

- `catalog/skills/shatter-doctor/SKILL.md` exists with frontmatter, body,
  and a sibling `metadata.json`.
- Skill is shipped in the `shatter` plugin and listed in marketplace.json.
- Skill works without a `shatter doctor` subcommand existing.
- A fixture test asserts the skill loads.

## In scope

- Binary verification (presence, runnable, version).
- Config schema check via parser-surfaced errors.
- Per-target integration verdict with proximate reason.
- Recommended remediation by pointing at other skills.

## Out of scope

- Running Shatter exploration (that is `run-shatter`).
- Modifying the project to fix issues (that is `add-shatter-target` and
  `install-shatter`).
- Comparing two diagnostic runs over time.

## Depends on

The shatterproof marketplace bootstrap, the `install-shatter` skill (for
binary-install remediation references), and the run-target discovery helper
that `run-shatter` ships with — once that helper lives under
`catalog/skills/run-shatter/scripts/run_targets.py`, `shatter-doctor` must
invoke it from that location.

title: pin-refute skill
description:
Add a `pin-refute` skill to the refute plugin in shatter-agents.

## Purpose

Pin `refute` as a project-managed dependency so collaborators and CI use a
known version rather than whatever happens to be on the user's PATH.

## Audience

Integrator. Run once per project.

## Behavior

The skill should:

- Detect whether the project uses Go modules with Go 1.24+. If yes, prefer
  the Go-tool dependency path:
  - `go get -tool github.com/shatterproof-ai/refute/cmd/refute@<version>`
  - Verify with `go tool refute version`.
- Otherwise, recommend a project-local release-binary install under
  `.bin/refute` or `tools/refute` (per `INSTALL.md`) with a version pinned in
  a small `tools/refute.version` file.
- Refuse to pin to a floating tag (`@latest`, `@main`). Require a concrete
  release tag and warn if the user supplies a continuous build tag.
- Show the resulting diff (e.g., `go.mod` change or version file creation)
  before writing.

## Smallest concrete shape

User in a Go 1.26 project says "pin refute". Skill picks the Go-tool path,
proposes `go get -tool github.com/shatterproof-ai/refute/cmd/refute@v0.1.x`,
shows the resulting go.mod diff, and on approval runs the command and
verifies with `go tool refute version`.

## Acceptance

- `catalog/skills/pin-refute/SKILL.md` exists.
- Skill is shipped in the `refute` plugin and listed in marketplace.json.
- Skill refuses floating tags.

## In scope

- Go-tool dependency for Go 1.24+ projects.
- Project-local pinned binary for non-Go projects.
- Diff-then-write user gate.

## Out of scope

- Installing language-server backends (covered by `install-refute`).
- Updating an existing pin (separate future skill or manual).
- Pinning across multiple projects in a monorepo (treat as one-per-project
  for v1).

## Depends on

The shatterproof marketplace bootstrap and the `install-refute` skill (for
the underlying install/verify primitives).

title: refute-rename skill
description:
Add a `refute-rename` skill to the refute plugin in shatter-agents.

## Purpose

Drive a single symbol-aware rename using `refute` with a strict preview-then-
apply discipline. The skill keeps the user in control of the actual edit and
treats the preview diff as the artifact for review.

## Audience

Downstream user. Run when the user wants an IDE-quality rename from the CLI
on a Go, Rust, or TypeScript codebase that has the right LSP backend
installed.

## Behavior

The skill should:

- Confirm the project's language and verify the relevant LSP backend is
  installed by running `refute doctor` and parsing its output.
- Take the old symbol name and new symbol name (and optionally a source file
  hint when symbol disambiguation is needed).
- Run `refute rename <args>` in preview mode and capture the diff.
- Show the user the diff and any backend warnings.
- On user approval, re-run with apply mode and confirm the edit by showing
  the resulting `git status` and a short summary.
- If the backend is missing or out of date, refuse to proceed and point at
  `refute doctor`'s recommended fix.

## Smallest concrete shape

User says "rename `Foo` to `Bar` in this Go package". Skill confirms gopls
is healthy via `refute doctor`, runs the rename in preview mode, shows the
diff, gets approval, applies, and reports the affected files.

## Acceptance

- `catalog/skills/refute-rename/SKILL.md` exists.
- Skill is shipped in the `refute` plugin and listed in marketplace.json.
- Skill enforces the preview-then-apply discipline.
- Skill refuses to proceed when the backend is missing or stale.

## In scope

- Single rename per invocation.
- Go, Rust, and TypeScript backends per refute's current support matrix.
- Preview diff as the artifact for user review.

## Out of scope

- Multi-step planned refactors (covered by `refute-from-plan`).
- Cross-language renames.
- Java/Kotlin (not claimed for refute v0.1).

## Depends on

The shatterproof marketplace bootstrap, the `install-refute` skill (for the
binary), and the `refute-doctor` skill (for the backend-health check the
rename skill reuses).

title: wire-shatter-ci skill
description:
Add a `wire-shatter-ci` skill to the shatter plugin in shatter-agents.

## Purpose

Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs Shatter on the project's integrated
targets, captures artifacts, and uploads them as a workflow artifact.

## Audience

Integrator. Run once per project to set up automated Shatter runs.

## Behavior

The skill should:

- Confirm at least one target is already integrated (via
  `run-shatter`'s helper). If none are integrated, recommend
  `add-shatter-target` first and stop.
- Detect the project's existing GitHub Actions setup (Node version, Go
  version, package manager) by inspecting `.github/workflows/` and the
  manifests already in the repo.
- Generate a new `.github/workflows/shatter.yml` that:
  - Installs the `shatter` binary using the published install script with a
    `BUILD=` tag pinned for repeatability.
  - Installs the project's existing language toolchains.
  - Runs `python3 -m shatter_agents.run_targets --root . --json` (or the
    `scripts/run_targets.py` invocation, depending on packaging).
  - Uploads the run directory as a workflow artifact.
- Show the diff before writing.
- Stop short of configuring branch-protection rules or required-status checks.

## Smallest concrete shape

User in a Go+TS repo with no Shatter workflow says "wire shatter into CI".
Skill produces a draft `shatter.yml` with the pinned binary install, the
right toolchains, the run command, and an artifact upload step. User
approves and the skill writes the file.

## Acceptance

- `catalog/skills/wire-shatter-ci/SKILL.md` exists.
- Skill is shipped in the `shatter` plugin and listed in marketplace.json.
- Generated workflow uses a pinned `BUILD=` tag, not "latest".

## In scope

- GitHub Actions only.
- Single workflow file, single job per OS by default.
- Artifact upload of the run directory.

## Out of scope

- Other CI systems (CircleCI, GitLab CI, Buildkite).
- Branch protection or required-status configuration.
- Posting results to PR comments (separate future skill).

## Depends on

The shatterproof marketplace bootstrap, the existing `run-shatter` skill,
and ideally `add-shatter-target` so the integrated-targets precondition is
easy to satisfy.

title: interpret-shatter-spec skill
description:
Add an `interpret-shatter-spec` skill to the shatter plugin in shatter-agents.

## Purpose

Explain a single Shatter spec JSON file (one function's exploration result)
in human terms. Lighter than `review-shatter-output`, which is meant for a
whole run and produces a multi-section review.

## Audience

Downstream user, ad hoc inspection. Useful when the user runs Shatter on a
single function and wants a short, focused explanation rather than a full
analyst review.

## Behavior

The skill should:

- Take a path to a spec JSON file (or stdin) and parse it.
- Identify the function's input domain splits, branch conditions, and any
  thrown errors or notable boundary cases.
- Produce a brief explanation (target ~100-200 words) of what the function
  appears to do, the 2-4 most representative cases, and any obvious
  ambiguities.
- Distinguish program behavior from likely tool issues using the same
  guidance as `review-shatter-output`.
- Reference `references/report-schema.md` only for the case format; this
  skill should not produce a full report.

## Smallest concrete shape

User passes a path to `shatter-artifacts/foo.spec.json`. Skill prints a short
markdown summary with one paragraph of overall interpretation and 2-4
bullet-point cases each with inputs and expected outputs.

## Acceptance

- `catalog/skills/interpret-shatter-spec/SKILL.md` exists.
- Skill is shipped in the `shatter` plugin and listed in marketplace.json.
- Output stays in the "single spec, short summary" lane and does not
  recapitulate the full `review-shatter-output` schema.

## In scope

- Single spec JSON input.
- Short human-readable interpretation.
- Lightweight reuse of the case-selection heuristics from
  `review-shatter-output`.

## Out of scope

- Whole-run reviews (use `review-shatter-output`).
- Markdown issue reports (use `report-shatter-issues`).
- Comparing two specs across runs (separate future skill).

## Depends on

The shatterproof marketplace bootstrap and the existing
`review-shatter-output` skill (for shared case-selection guidance and the
report-schema reference).

title: install-shatter skill
description:
Add an `install-shatter` skill to the shatter plugin in shatter-agents.

## Purpose

Help a downstream user install the `shatter` binary and run `shatter init` to
opt a project into persistent Shatter state.

## Audience

Downstream user, first-time bootstrap path. Not for shatter repo maintainers.

## Behavior

The skill should:

- Detect the user's platform (Linux/macOS) and recommend the correct install
  path: continuous binary via the published install script, pinned `BUILD=`
  tag for CI, or build-from-source for contributors.
- Run or guide the user through the install command, defaulting to
  `~/.local/bin` unless the user sets `INSTALL_DIR`.
- Verify install with `shatter --help` and surface any missing toolchain
  prerequisites (libclang, Node, Go) when build-from-source is chosen.
- After install, offer to run `shatter init` in the current project root and
  explain what `.shatter/config.yaml` does.
- Stop short of registering Shatter targets in the project — that is the job
  of the separate `add-shatter-target` skill.

## Smallest concrete shape

User says "install shatter and set this repo up". Skill picks the platform,
runs the install script, verifies the binary, then runs `shatter init` and
shows the user the resulting `.shatter/config.yaml`.

title: refute-from-plan skill
description:
Add a `refute-from-plan` skill to the refute plugin in shatter-agents.

> **Triage status:** Filed as triage-only. Plan-file format is proposed but
> not ratified; do not start implementation until the plan format is settled.

## Purpose

Execute a planned refactor — an ordered list of renames or moves — as a
sequence of refute operations with per-step review. Lets a user or another
agent capture the plan first, then drive the edits deterministically.

## Audience

Integrator and downstream user. Used after a separate planning step
produces an ordered list of operations.

## Unresolved questions (must be answered before leaving triage)

- Plan file format: YAML, JSON, or both? Schema validation tool?
- What does "stop the plan" mean for already-applied operations — leave them
  applied (current proposal) or roll back via VCS? If rollback, by what
  mechanism?
- Disambiguation semantics of the `file` hint must match `refute-rename`
  exactly. Specify the contract once `refute-rename` lands.

## Behavior (proposal, pending triage resolution)

The skill should:

- Accept a plan file (YAML or JSON) listing operations in order. Each
  operation has: kind (`rename` for v1), old name, new name, optional file
  hint, and an optional note.
- Validate the plan structure before doing any work; refuse on unknown
  operation kinds.
- For each operation in order:
  - Run `refute` in preview mode.
  - Show the diff and the operation's note.
  - Pause for user approval before applying.
  - Apply on approval. On rejection, stop the plan and report which
    operations applied and which did not.
- Produce a final summary listing applied operations and any skipped ones.

## Plan file shape (v1 proposal)

```yaml
operations:
  - kind: rename
    old: OldName
    new: NewName
    file: path/to/file.go   # optional disambiguation
    note: rationale          # optional, shown at preview time
```

## Smallest concrete shape

User has a plan file with three Go renames. Skill validates the plan, then
walks operation 1, 2, 3 — preview, approve, apply each — and reports a
3/3 summary.

## Acceptance

- `catalog/skills/refute-from-plan/SKILL.md` exists.
- Skill is shipped in the `refute` plugin and listed in marketplace.json.
- Skill stops on first rejection rather than skipping ahead.
- Plan validation runs before any edits.

## In scope

- Ordered execution of a YAML or JSON plan file.
- `rename` operation kind in v1.
- Per-operation preview-then-apply with explicit user gate.

## Out of scope

- Move/extract/inline operations (future versions).
- Plan authoring (planning happens upstream of this skill).
- Parallel or batched application without per-step gates.

## Depends on

The shatterproof marketplace bootstrap and the `refute-rename` skill (for
the preview-then-apply primitive).
notes: Session discussion (2026-05-20): the per-step human-approval loop is questionable — no human will write a YAML rename plan. The original framing assumes a two-agent pipeline (one plans, one executes) but that is not stated explicitly and no concrete scenario exists that motivates it. The 'explicit user gate' at each step may not make sense if the executor is an agent. Before leaving triage, a concrete refactoring scenario is needed to validate whether this skill is the right abstraction at all. It may be that higher-order refactorings are better handled differently.
